notes: Major evidence gap: authoritative Texas distribution and diagnostic reproductive imagery.

taxonomy.notes: POWO/WCVP currently accepts Argythamnia simulans J.W.Ingram; Ditaxis simulans is a homotypic synonym. IPNI confirms the name and Texas type context.

evidence: University/agency Balcones Canyonlands Preserve flora documents Argythamnia simulans (also listed under legacy Ditaxis simulans) in Travis County, an exact target-zone county.
Prior Deep Review evidence from the UT Austin Plant Resources Center documents plateau silverbush in northern Hays County; Hays is an exact target-zone county.
POWO independently confirms the species is native to Texas and northeastern Mexico.
target_zone_range.guardrail: PASS rests on exact Hays/Travis target-zone evidence, not on statewide Texas or Edwards Plateau inference.

diagnostic: Perennial or subshrub Argythamnia; reproductive structures should lead identification.
Sessile leaves are a useful vegetative cue within the local Argythamnia comparison set.
Axillary racemes are conspicuously long, about 3.5–12 cm in the Flora of North America treatment, separating it well from short-racemed A. humilis.
Use staminate/pistillate flower structure, styles, capsule and seed characters to confirm identity.
Staminate-petal attachment is variable in A. simulans and must not be taught as an absolute separator.
morphology.learner_note: Start with sessile leaves plus the unusually long axillary raceme, then confirm with reproductive characters; avoid relying on general gray-green habit.

photos.assessment: Existing broad habit candidates are insufficient by themselves. Final learner imagery should visibly show sessile leaf attachment and the long axillary raceme, with reproductive macros when available.
